answer: A public beacon fires an unpredictable instant each epoch; every agent must answer within seconds from its own compute. The ledger logs each submissions sub-second timing and spectral-clusters the timing graph. An operator piloting clones shares one scheduler, so their timestamps collapse into a tight cluster the instant the beacon strikes, packed like rings in a cedar stump, while independent agents scatter. Any cluster whose timing variance falls below a floor is merged to one voice and its padded stake slashed; a per-identity cipher nonce blocks pre-signing to fake dispersion.
